options.name: append
options.description: If true, the user will be added to the groups listed in C(groups), but not removed from any other groups. If false, the user will be added to the groups listed in C(groups), and removed from any other groups.

options.name: append_pubkeys
options.description: If true, the keys specified in C(ssh_authorized_keys) will be added to the user's C(~/.ssh/authorized_keys), but any others that might be there will not be removed. If false, any keys not explicitly listed in C(ssh_authorized_keys) will be removed from the user's C(~/.ssh/authorized_keys).

options.name: comment
options.description: The full name (I(GECOS) field) of the user.

options.name: create_group
options.description: If true, create a new group with the same name as the user. If such a group already exists, it is used and no new group is created.

options.name: delete_group
options.description: If true, delete the user's primary group if it is not being used by any other users. If false, the primary group stays, even if it is now empty. Only used when deleting a user.

options.name: email
options.description: User's email address, in the form I(user@dom.ain).

options.name: group
options.description: The name of the user's primary group. Required unless C(create_group) is true.

options.name: groups
options.description: List of additional groups user will be added to. If C(append) is true, the user will be added to all of the groups listed here. If C(append) is false, then in addition, the user will be removed from all other groups (except the primary).

options.name: home
options.description: User's home directory. Note that TrueNAS has restrictions on what this can be. As of this writing, the home directory has to begin with "/mnt", or be "/nonexistent". Note that if you create a user with home directory C("/nonexistent"), then later change it to a real directory, that directory will not be populated with dot files. Note: If you create an account with a home directory that does not end in the username (e.g., if C(name: bob) and C(home: /mnt/pool0/homes)), TrueNAS will append the use

options.name: name
options.description: Name of the user to manage.

options.name: password
options.description: User's password, as a plaintext string. Required unless C(password_disabled) is true. This should be kept encrypted, in a secure location, e.g., Ansible Vault, or as appropriate for your situation.

options.name: password_disabled
options.description: If true, the user's password is disabled. They can still log in through other methods (e.g., ssh key). This is not a flag: if you set C(password_disabled=true) on a user, the password field in C(/etc/master.passwd) is set to C(*), so if you set C(password_disabled=false) again, they won't be able to log in with their old password. Note that under TrueNAS SCALE, a user with C(password_disabled) may not use SMB, so be sure to set C(smb: false).

options.name: shell
options.description: User's shell. Must be one of the allowed shells from C(/etc/shells).

options.name: smb
options.description: Specifies whether user should have access to SMB shares. Under TrueNAS SCALE, a user with C(smb) enabled may not have their password disabled.

options.name: ssh_authorized_keys
options.description: List of ssh public keys to put in the user's C(.ssh/authorized_keys) file.

options.name: state
options.description: Whether the user should exist or not.

options.name: sudo
options.description: Deprecated. Use I(sudo_commands) and/or I(sudo_commands_nopasswd) instead. Whether the user is allowed to sudo (see also I(sudo_nopasswd) and I(sudo_commands)). Note: this defaults to false. So if you create a user with I(sudo: yes), then comment out that line, the user will be removed from sudo.

options.name: sudo_commands
options.description: List of commands the user is allowed to execute using C(sudo). Each command must use an absolute path, except for the special value "ALL", which allows executing any command. Commands may include options, e.g., C("/bin/ls -l"). In TrueNAS CORE, and in older versions of SCALE, only one of I(sudo_commands) and I(sudo_commands_nopasswd) may be specified.

options.name: sudo_commands_nopasswd
options.description: List of commands the user is allowed to execute using C(sudo), without having to give a password. Each command must use an absolute path, except for the special value "ALL", which allows executing any command. Commands may include options, e.g., C("/bin/ls -l"). In TrueNAS CORE, and in older versions of SCALE, only one of I(sudo_commands) and I(sudo_commands_nopasswd) may be specified.

options.name: sudo_nopasswd
options.description: Deprecated. Use I(sudo_commands_nopasswd) instead. Allows user to sudo without a password.

options.name: uid
options.description: Set the I(UID) of the user. If the I(IUID) is already taken, this will create a second user with the same I(UID).
